messages.subject: stepwiseqtlF
parts:
Hi everyone,

I've been playing around a bit with the 'funqtl' package and I have a few questions about the stepwiseqtlF function. For one dataset I'm working with, when I attempt to perform stepwiseqtlF model selection using this function call:

> d.qtlslod <- stepwiseqtlF(d.fg.cr.obj, pheno.cols = d.phe, max.qtl = 3, usec = "slod", method = "hk", penalties = c(1,1,1) )

I receive the following error message:

 -Initial scan
** new best ** (pLOD increased by 1.1134)
    no.qtl =  1   pLOD = 1.113447   formula: y ~ Q1 
 -Step 1 
 ---Scanning for additive qtl
Error in makeqtl(cross, chr, pos, qtl.name = qtl.name, what = what) : 
  Input chr and qtl.name must have the same length.
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In max(lod[upper.tri(lod)], na.rm = TRUE) :
  no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
2: In max(lod[lower.tri(lod)], na.rm = TRUE) :
  no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
3: In max(out[, 3], na.rm = TRUE) :
  no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

For another dataset with almost identical structure (datasets were derived from the same source and divided by treatment using grep) the stepwiseqtlF function returns values without error or warnings but the cofactors selected are quite different than one would expect based on the examination of plotlod(scanone_output) results and resulting model selected using the stepwiseqtl function on a single representative time point. 

I've looked into the underlying code of the stepwiseqtlF function but I'm not totally sure what aspect is fouling things up. Any help or suggestions are greatly appreciated. Thanks!

Max
